proofs.text: Write a proof carrying `@env(windows)` and commit a passing record from `linux`; verify the rule is not `Recorded`, that `missing_env` is exactly `["windows"]` and that the reasons carry `windows: no record yet`; then commit a passing record from `windows` and verify the rule is `Recorded`

reasons: PROOF-6 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: A proof carrying `@env` is proved only by a record from that operating system: the rule stays out of Recorded, names the operating system under `missing_env`, and gives the reason `<os>: no record yet` rather than taking an eighth state

tests.body:
def test_an_env_proof_needs_a_record_from_that_operating_system(self,
                                                                   project):
        project.spec(
            '# Feature: login\n\n## Rules\n\n- RULE-1: Files lock\n\n'
            '## Proof\n\n- PROOF-1 (RULE-1): Lock a file; verify a second open '
            'returns 0 handles @env(windows)\n')
        project.record([{'id': 'PROOF-1', 'rule': 'RULE-1', 'status': 'pass'}],
                       os_name='linux')
        rule = project.rule('RULE-1')
        assert rule['state'] != 'Recorded'
        assert rule['missing_env'] == ['windows'], rule
        assert 'windows: no record yet' in rule['reasons'], rule
        project.record([{'id': 'PROOF-1', 'rule': 'RULE-1', 'status': 'pass'}],
                       os_name='windows')
        assert project.rule('RULE-1')['state'] == 'Recorded'
tests.name: test_an_env_proof_needs_a_record_from_that_operating_system
